Whole body oxygen delivery is the amount of oxygen delivered to the tissues per unit time. It is calculated using the formula:  

\[
\text{Whole body oxygen delivery} = \text{Cardiac output} \times \text{Oxygen content of arterial blood}
\]

- **Cardiac output** is the volume of blood pumped by the heart per minute (typically ~5 L/min at rest).  
- **Oxygen content of arterial blood** is the amount of oxygen carried by the blood, which depends on hemoglobin concentration and oxygen saturation. For example, if arterial blood has an oxygen content of 200 mL/L and cardiac output is 5 L/min, whole body oxygen delivery would be:  

\[
5 \, \text{L/min} \times 200 \, \text{mL/L} = 1000 \, \text{mL/min} \, (\text{or} \, 1 \, \text{L/min})
